title: Haiku Sandbox Problem Solving T2 HowTo
desc: T2 domain tier. Brief templates for Haiku prototype + wkcodex apply. When to prototype vs direct apply. Anti-patterns.
steps: HAIKU BRIEF TEMPLATE: 'Problem: [1 sentence]. Write new file /tmp/proof-X.ps1 (or .cs). Input: [exact values]. Expected output: [exact values]. Print PASS/FAIL. Do NOT touch existing source.' Short, unambiguous, sandboxed.

WKCODEX BRIEF TEMPLATE (after Haiku confirms PASS): 'File: csharp/src/.../X.cs. Change: old=[exact text] new=[exact text]. Build: wkappbot-pub build.cmd. Smoke: wkappbot cdp open https://example.com. Commit with keyword [X].'

WHEN TO PROTOTYPE FIRST: algorithm uncertain, multiple approaches possible, subtle timing/race condition, logic spans 3+ conditions. WHEN TO APPLY DIRECTLY: Sonnet already understands fix from reading source, change <= 5 lines, trivial rename/constant change.

ANTI-PATTERNS: (A) 'Haiku, find bug in CdpClient.cs and fix it' = diagnose+edit = context overload. (B) 'wkcodex, fix the retry bug' = vague = wrong result. (C) Sonnet uses Edit tool directly on complex source = PATTERN 6 violation.
PARALLEL PATTERN: when solution has 2 candidate approaches, fire Haiku × 2 simultaneously (each builds different proof). Sonnet picks winner. Faster than sequential and no risk to original source.
author: claude
